items.title: Three secret lists disagree — reconcile into one signed-off list
items.notes: The list of secrets actually marked for replication, the manual spreadsheet, and the runtime logical names used by secrets-init do not match. Two adjudication secrets had no replica in us-east-2 and killed test #2 (2026-08-28). A replica secret keeps the same NAME, so a name that resolves in us-east-1 and not in us-east-2 means nobody ever enabled replication for it. Blocker for test #3: one CSV, signed by claims + platform leads, verified against us-east-2.

items.title: Remittance Aurora measured a 118-min RPA against a 30-min configuration
items.notes: The remittance cluster is the last Tier-0 store on third-party point-in-time recovery rather than continuous replication. In test #2 its recovery point came from a different sync than the object and queue points, so the realized RPA was 118 min. Two ways out, and the decision is dec_mechanisms': move it to an Aurora Global Database like the adjudication cluster (sub-second lag, cost of a warm secondary), or keep point-in-time recovery and prove aligned recovery points as a gate in every test. Until one of them is done, the workspace RPA is this component's number.

items.title: Kinesis claim/transaction streams not in recovery scope
items.notes: Open question: does adjudication need the streams to ANSWER a claim, or only for downstream analytics? If the former, this is a hidden blocker for the success bar. Answer in writing before test #3 (Phase 0 item 12).

items.title: Partner allowlist for recovery-region egress IPs is manual
items.notes: The clearinghouse allowlists our egress IPs by hand via a support ticket (days of lead time). In a real event, claims fail at the partner edge until it clears. Options: pre-register recovery egress IPs now, or reserve static EIPs in us-east-2 and register once.

items.title: Redis pharmacy/remittance is a stale include in recovery scope
items.notes: Flagged 'partial' with unknown replication. Likely a rebuildable cache, but nobody has confirmed with the service owners whether pharmacy-service tolerates a cold start of it — and AWS Backup does not cover ElastiCache at all, so "it is backed up" is not an available answer. Confirm, then either drop it from scope, document the rebuild path and its warm-up cost, or put it on Global Datastore.

items.title: Public DNS flip is manual
items.notes: Accepted for now: Phase-1 tests never touch DNS, and a manual flip is acceptable for the first game day. Revisit when choosing orchestration — Route 53 health-check failover records, ARC routing controls and ARC Region Switch are the peer options — see decision dec_orchestration.

items.title: DR readiness dashboard v0 not built
items.notes: Runbook gates (replication green, nodes Ready, secrets clean, edge 200) are checked by hand across four consoles. A single dashboard would cut minutes off every gate and make the preflight checklist honest.
